items.prompt: An immutable R × C matrix must answer many axis-aligned rectangle-sum queries. Which state most directly supports constant-time queries after preprocessing?
constraints: Rectangle boundaries may arrive in arbitrary order.
No matrix cell is updated after preprocessing.

options.text: A padded 2D prefix P where P[r][c] stores the sum of rows [0, r) and columns [0, c).
One moving sum for the current row only.
All matrix values sorted into a one-dimensional list.
One minimum value per row.

feedback.reason: A rectangle is bounded independently on two axes, so reusable cumulative state must summarize every row-column boundary pair.

blocks.text: A 2D prefix stores the sum of every top-left half-open rectangle: P[r][c] covers rows below r and columns below c. For an inclusive query (r1, c1) through (r2, c2), start with P[r2 + 1][c2 + 1], subtract the region above it with P[r1][c2 + 1] and the region left of it with P[r2 + 1][c1], then add P[r1][c1] because that top-left overlap was subtracted twice. Thus four stored boundary states isolate any rectangle in constant time. A row window, sorted cells, or row minima loses column boundaries, original geometry, or additive information.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.one_row_window: A row-only window cannot isolate arbitrary vertical boundaries or combine many rows in constant time.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sorted_cells: Sorting destroys cell coordinates, so a rectangle no longer corresponds to a contiguous geometric region.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.row_minima: Per-row minima are neither additive nor sufficient to reconstruct a rectangle sum.

items.prompt: Under the padded convention, what must P[r][c] mean for the standard four-term rectangle formula to be valid?
constraints: P has dimensions (R + 1) × (C + 1).
Row 0 and column 0 are zero sentinels.

options.text: Only the value at matrix cell (r, c).
The sum of matrix cells with row < r and column < c.
The sum of whichever rectangle was queried most recently.
The sum of the r × c smallest matrix values.

feedback.reason: Each prefix state must own a fixed top-left half-open rectangle so overlapping regions can be added and removed consistently.

blocks.text: P[r][c] covers rows [0, r) and columns [0, c). This stable geometric invariant lets the query use one bottom-right prefix, subtract two outside strips, and add back their double-subtracted overlap. A dynamic current rectangle or sorted rank has no fixed spatial ownership for inclusion-exclusion.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.single_cell_value: One cell does not summarize the top-left region, so four such values cannot reconstruct an arbitrary rectangle sum.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.current_rectangle_window: A current rectangle changes meaning between queries and provides no reusable state at all boundary pairs.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sorted_rank_sum: Value rank ignores coordinates. Inclusion-exclusion requires geometric containment, not sorted magnitude.

items.prompt: Order the conceptual inclusion-exclusion operations for the inclusive rectangle with corners (r1, c1) and (r2, c2), using padded P.
constraints: P[r][c] sums rows [0, r) and columns [0, c).
Score is based on preserved adjacent relations.

elements.text: Start with P[r2 + 1][c2 + 1], the top-left region through the query’s bottom-right cell.
Subtract P[r1][c2 + 1], the rows above the query.
Subtract P[r2 + 1][c1], the columns left of the query.
Add P[r1][c1], the top-left overlap subtracted twice.
Interpret the remaining contribution as exactly the requested rectangle.

feedback.reason: The two outside strips are removed independently, and their shared overlap must be restored once.

blocks.text: The bottom-right prefix includes the target plus cells above and left of it. Inclusion-exclusion removes those two outside regions while compensating for their overlap.

items: Take P[r2 + 1][c2 + 1], which covers every row and column through the query's lower-right cell.
Subtract P[r1][c2 + 1] to remove all covered cells above row r1.
Subtract P[r2 + 1][c1] to remove all covered cells left of column c1.
Add P[r1][c1] because the top-left outside region belonged to both removed strips and was subtracted twice.
Interpret the remaining cells as exactly rows r1..r2 and columns c1..c2.

blocks.title: The overlap needs one restoration
blocks.text: Stopping after the two subtractions removes the top-left outside region twice. The final positive term is the inclusion-exclusion correction, not an optional boundary adjustment.

items.prompt: Which formula returns the inclusive rectangle (r1, c1) through (r2, c2) under the padded half-open prefix convention?
constraints: P has a zero sentinel row and column.

feedback.reason: The padded boundaries convert both inclusive lower-right coordinates to +1 and inclusion-exclusion restores the doubly removed top-left overlap.

blocks.text: The first term includes the rectangle plus outside top and left regions. The next two remove those strips, and the last adds back their overlap. Omitting +1 excludes the bottom row or right column, while using only two diagonal prefixes cannot remove the L-shaped outside area.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.omit_overlap_add: The top-left outside region belongs to both subtracted strips, so it would be removed twice without the compensating addition.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.use_data_indices_directly: P uses exclusive boundaries. Direct data indices stop before r2 and c2, excluding requested cells.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.two_term_diagonal: Subtracting one top-left prefix removes only a rectangle, not the separate top and left strips contained in the bottom-right prefix.

items.prompt: Why is one moving rectangular window not equivalent to a 2D prefix for arbitrary rectangle queries?
constraints: Queries can jump between unrelated row and column boundaries.
The matrix is immutable.

options.text: A window rectangle is mathematically forbidden from changing size.
The 2D prefix is useful because all prefix entries are sorted.
The 2D prefix stores no state, unlike a window.
A 2D prefix answers from four stored boundary states independent of the previous query, while moving a rectangle may cross many rows and columns.

feedback.reason: Prefix queries are stateless random access over precomputed geometry; a moving rectangle’s update cost depends on how its prior boundaries change.

blocks.text: Four reads and fixed arithmetic isolate any rectangle, regardless of query order. A moving rectangular window can be efficient for a controlled sweep of fixed shape, but arbitrary jumps can require updating many entering and leaving cells. The prefix gains predictable O(1) queries by storing O(RC) cumulative state.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.rectangles_cannot_move: Moving windows can change position and sometimes size. The issue is the cost and invariant of those updates, not a mathematical prohibition.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.prefix_values_sorted: Negative cells can make prefix values non-monotonic. Sortedness is unrelated to inclusion-exclusion.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.prefix_no_memory: A padded 2D prefix stores (R + 1)(C + 1) entries, which is O(RC) extra space.

items.prompt: Why must matrix cells remain in their original coordinates when building a 2D prefix for rectangle queries?
constraints: Queries identify rectangles by row and column indices.
Cell values may be in any order and may be negative.

options.text: The prefix summarizes geometric top-left regions, so sorting cells would change rectangle membership.
Row sums are valid only when each row is sorted.
A 2D prefix cannot contain negative intermediate sums.
Inclusion-exclusion requires every column to be nondecreasing.

feedback.reason: 2D prefix correctness is spatial, not order-statistical: every state is tied to fixed coordinates.

blocks.text: Addition and inclusion-exclusion work for arbitrary signs and value order. What cannot change is which cell lies inside each top-left region and each query rectangle. Sorting rows, columns, or all cells would answer a different geometric problem.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.addition_needs_sorted_rows: Addition has no sorted-row precondition. The recurrence uses neighboring cumulative regions regardless of value order.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.negative_cells_forbidden: Prefix entries may be negative. Inclusion-exclusion remains an exact algebraic identity.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.columns_must_be_monotonic: Monotonic columns are irrelevant. The formula relies on containment and cancellation of regions.

items.prompt: Select preprocessing time, one-query time, and extra space for a separate padded 2D prefix over an R × C matrix.
constraints: Each prefix entry is computed in O(1) from neighboring states and one cell.
A query reads four prefix entries.
The input matrix is not counted as extra space.

feedback.reason: Every cell contributes to one prefix entry, each query uses four states, and the padded table stores one state per row-column boundary pair.

blocks.text: The padded table has (R + 1)(C + 1) entries. Computing each non-sentinel entry once from constant neighboring state gives O(RC) preprocessing time, and retaining all entries gives O(RC) extra space. Each query performs four reads and a fixed three additions or subtractions, so query time is O(1).

blocks.title: Why the other offered bounds are wrong
blocks.text: Preprocessing is not O(R + C) because every one of RC cells contributes, O(RC log(RC)) adds sorting or logarithmic work that is absent, and O(R²C²) rescans rectangles that the recurrence avoids. Query time has no search, row/column scan, or matrix scan, rejecting the logarithmic, O(R + C), and O(RC) alternatives. Space is not O(1) or O(R + C) because one state is stored per row-column boundary pair, and not O(R²C²) because there is only one padded table.

items.prompt: Which requirement transfers directly to the same 2D prefix mechanism after changing each cell’s contribution?
constraints: The matrix is immutable.
Queries ask about arbitrary axis-aligned rectangles.

options.text: Find the median cell value by subtracting four scalar prefix sums.
Count obstacle cells in each rectangle by prefixing 1 for an obstacle and 0 otherwise.
Change cells online while keeping an unchanged static 2D prefix.
Find the largest rectangle satisfying a constraint using one four-term query only.

feedback.reason: A 0/1 cell contribution remains additive over rectangles, so the same four-term inclusion-exclusion isolates the count.

blocks.text: The geometry and boundary formula stay unchanged; only the per-cell contribution becomes an indicator. A scalar sum does not encode a median, online updates stale many prefix entries, and optimizing over all possible rectangles requires a search or different invariant beyond one region query.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.rectangle_median: Four scalar sums retain only total magnitude, not the distribution needed for a median.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.online_cell_updates: Changing one cell affects every prefix region below and to its right. A static table cannot remain correct without updates or a dynamic structure.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.largest_valid_rectangle: A four-term query evaluates one supplied rectangle. It does not choose the best rectangle among many candidates.

items.prompt: For an n by m grid, what dimensions make a 2D exclusive prefix matrix uniform for edge queries?

options.text: (n+1) by (m+1), including zero row and zero column boundaries.
n by m, matching the number of grid cells exactly.
(n+2) by (m+2), because each cell needs two padding rows.
max(n,m) by max(n,m), padding the shorter dimension.

feedback.reason: The extra row and column represent empty prefixes before row zero and column zero.

blocks.text: With exclusive boundaries, grid cell (r,c) contributes when building P[r+1][c+1]. The padding makes rectangles touching either outer edge use the same four-corner formula.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.n_by_m: Without padding, edge rectangles require special-case indices or risk negative access.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.n_plus_two: One empty boundary per axis is sufficient.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.square_max: The representation should preserve both original dimensions, not force a square.

items.prompt: How many prefix-matrix corner values are needed to answer one axis-aligned rectangle sum with inclusion-exclusion?

options.text: Four: the bottom-right total, two excluded strips, and the restored top-left overlap.
Two, because a rectangle has only two diagonal corners.
One, because the prefix already stores the requested rectangle exactly.
One value per cell inside the query rectangle.

feedback.reason: Two subtractions remove the regions above and left of the target, and their overlap must be added back once.

blocks.text: This is the 2D analogue of a one-dimensional prefix difference, with inclusion-exclusion accounting for the overlap of the two removed prefixes.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.two: The two excluded regions overlap, requiring a fourth correction term.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.one: A global prefix contains the target plus outside regions.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.all_cells: Scanning cells would lose the constant-time query benefit.

items.prompt: Which inclusion-exclusion formula gives the sum of rectangle [r1..r2]x[c1..c2] using a zero-padded 2D prefix P?
constraints: P[i][j] sums rows and columns before i,j.
The rectangle indices are inclusive.

options.explanation: Subtract the top and left strips and add their overlap back.

options.text: Use total minus only the top strip and ignore the left strip.
options.explanation: That leaves unrelated cells in the result.

options.text: Subtract all four corner prefixes so the overlap is removed twice.
options.explanation: The overlap must be added once after two subtractions.

options.text: Use P[r2][c2] because the prefix already starts at the rectangle's top-left.
options.explanation: A global prefix includes cells outside the query rectangle.

feedback.reason: Two-dimensional range sums require two subtractions and one overlap correction.

blocks.text: The padded indices eliminate negative-boundary branches. Inclusion-exclusion removes the area above and left of the rectangle, then restores the doubly removed top-left overlap.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.three_terms: That leaves unrelated cells in the result.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.subtract_overlap: The overlap must be added once after two subtractions.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.one_term: A global prefix includes cells outside the query rectangle.

items.prompt: Why does adding an extra zero row and column simplify 2D prefix construction?
constraints: Queries may touch row 0 or column 0.
The prefix recurrence uses i−1 and j−1.

options.text: Padded zeros make the recurrence and inclusion-exclusion uniform at the matrix boundaries without negative-index special cases.
options.explanation: The empty prefix before the first row or column is represented explicitly.

options.text: Padding doubles every real matrix cell so sums are larger but easier to compare.
options.explanation: Padding adds only zero entries and changes no real sum.

options.text: The extra column stores the original first column so it need not be read.
options.explanation: It represents an empty prefix, not a copy of data.

options.text: Padding sorts rows and columns before prefix construction.
options.explanation: Prefix sums preserve input order and values.

feedback.reason: A zero border is a representation choice that turns boundary cases into the same recurrence.

blocks.text: For P[i+1][j+1], include the current cell, top prefix, left prefix, and subtract the diagonal overlap. The extra border supplies valid zeros when i or j is zero.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.double_area: Padding adds only zero entries and changes no real sum.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.avoid_columns: It represents an empty prefix, not a copy of data.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sort_matrix: Prefix sums preserve input order and values.

items.prompt: What input validation is needed before computing a 2D prefix rectangle query?
constraints: The query specifies two row bounds and two column bounds.
The output contract defines whether bounds are inclusive.

options.text: Normalize or reject r1>r2 and c1>c2 according to the contract, then apply the matching inclusive or half-open formula.
options.explanation: Formula indices depend on both order and endpoint semantics.

options.text: Always swap reversed bounds because every rectangle query is unordered.
options.explanation: Some contracts treat reversed ranges as invalid rather than normalize them.

options.text: Use the same formula for inclusive and exclusive bounds because prefixes are cumulative.
Sort matrix values within the rectangle before summing.
options.explanation: Sorting changes neither bounds semantics nor the required sum.

feedback.reason: Coordinate and endpoint semantics are part of the query contract.

blocks.text: A correct prefix formula cannot repair reversed or mismatched bounds. Validate or normalize explicitly, and translate inclusive ranges to padded prefix indices consistently.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.swap_always: Some contracts treat reversed ranges as invalid rather than normalize them.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sort_values: Sorting changes neither bounds semantics nor the required sum.

items.prompt: A matrix receives point updates between rectangle-sum queries. Why is a static 2D prefix array no longer automatically optimal?
constraints: Queries must reflect updates.
The matrix can be large.

options.text: One point update changes a rectangular suffix of prefix values, so naive repair can be O(rows*cols); a dynamic structure may be needed.
Only one prefix cell changes because prefixes store local cells.
options.explanation: Each later prefix includes the updated cell.

options.text: Updates can be ignored until the final query because prefixes describe the original matrix.
Rebuild the full prefix matrix after every update without counting the rebuild.
options.explanation: Rebuild cost is part of the workload.

feedback.reason: Static 2D prefixes are excellent for immutable matrices but have wide update dependencies.

blocks.text: If updates are frequent, a 2D Fenwick tree or segment structure can trade memory and logarithmic factors for dynamic correctness. If updates are rare, rebuild cost may still be acceptable and should be stated.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.local_prefix: Each later prefix includes the updated cell.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.rebuild_free: Rebuild cost is part of the workload.
